items.headline: Qwen3.5-9B on document benchmarks: where it beats frontier models and where it doesn't.
items.summary: We run an open document AI benchmark. 20 models, 9,000+ real documents. Just added all four Qwen3.5 sizes (0.8B to 9B). Now we have per-task breakdowns for every model. You can see the results here : idp-leaderboard.org  Where all Qwen wins or matches: OlmOCR (text extraction from messy scans, dense PDFs, multi-column layouts): Qwen3.5-9B: 78.1 Qwen3.5-4B: 77.2 Gemini 3.1 Pro: 74.6 Claude Sonnet 4.6: 74.4 Qwen3.5-2B: 73.7 GPT-5.4: 73.4 9B and 4B are ahead of every frontier model on raw tex

items.headline: To See is Not to Master: Teaching LLMs to Use Private Libraries for Code Generation
items.summary:

items.headline: A local-first personal database you can extend with apps and manage with AI
items.summary:
Hello all. I'm sharing this project (Superego, see on GitHub) I've been working on for way too long at this point, hoping to get some feedback and some early adopters.
As the title says, Superego is:

a database where you can store almost anything about your life;
which you can extend with snippets of TypeScript/React to build small personal apps for yourself (you can also vibe-code them);
which you can manage with its AI assistant (bring-your-own LLM).
